proposals.relationship: Hahn credits Genovese’s undergraduate teaching with transforming his commitment to rigorous historical scholarship and continues to use Genovese’s analyses of power and change in his own teaching.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2012 retrospectiveP2–3 identifies Rise of Modern Capitalism and the intellectual force of Genovese’s lectures;P11 explicitly retains lasting pedagogical debt. This is stronger than shared institution or generic student biography. P5 praises Roll, Jordan, Roll while serious objections remain elsewhere; no endorsement of every position or erased political divergence.

proposals.relationship: Hahn explicitly identifies Thompson’s social history, alongside Herbert Gutman’s, as a formative influence on his own historical approach.
proposals.evidence_note: Own edited2026 transcriptP4 is explicit influence testimony. The1960s describes the social history named, not an independently established first-reading date or direct teaching/mentorship by Thompson. Gutman has no endpoint and retains shared credit. Neither Thompson’s originals nor a complete2003 book were freshly read.

proposals.relationship: Hahn draws on Du Bois’s general-strike interpretation of enslaved people as political actors when explaining his own Civil War slave-rebellion argument.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2009 first answer explicitly invokes Black Reconstruction to support this interpretation, while saying agreement on political agency does not require adopting Du Bois’s Marxism.2026 P36 returns to the brave, long-neglected political assertion. Resource use, not a claim to fresh complete reading of Du Bois, nor endorsement of an uncontested largest-rebellion ranking.

proposals.relationship: Hahn questions Foner’s optimistic tendency about what Lincoln might have achieved in Reconstruction had he survived.
proposals.evidence_note: Own reviewP46 explicitly states this disagreement and leaves the counterfactual debatable. Extensive praise for Foner’s contextual and policy history remainsP5–7/18/35; criticism does not say Foner ignored enslaved initiative. Book original unread.13January online and3February2011 print dates distinguished.

proposals.relationship: Hahn challenges the Genoveses’ treatment of a unified master-class mind, arguing that their limited elite sample does not establish wider hegemony and leaves gender and enslaved participants insufficiently analysed.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2006 reviewP22–26 targets The Mind of the Master Class jointly authored by Elizabeth Fox-Genovese and Eugene Genovese; she lacks endpoint but her authorship and shared responsibility remain explicit. P15/18 praise its learned, often lively account and transatlantic range. This specific book criticism coexists with2012 gratitude to Eugene; not a deduction from political estrangement. Original book unread.
